To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the photophysical properties of new o-carbane derivatives incorporating different fluorophores have been studied, and the fluorescence can be tuned by changing the substituents on the adjacent C-cluster.
the fluorescence of o-carboranes can be tuned by changing the substituents at the Ccluster, but not by attaching different fluorophore groups to the Ccluster.

1) fluorene-containing o-carboranes show moderate fluorescence quantum yields; 2) fluorophores attached to the C-cluster are not fluorescent at room temperature; 3) anthracenyl groups bonded to o-carboranes are highly fluorescent in CH2Cl 2; and 4) the fluorescence intensity of anthracenyl-containing o-carborane is related to the length of the bond between the fluorophore and the Ccluster.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of o-carboranes with fluorophores attached to the Ccluster.
the design and synthesis of new fluorescent compounds containing o-carborane moieties.
the synthesis and study of the photophysical properties of a series of new carborane derivatives containing fluorene or anthracene as fluorophore units.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the presence of the fluorophore on the Ccluster is the most significant factor affecting the photophysical properties of these compounds, whereas the nature of the substituent on Ccluster has only a secondary effect.
the fluorescence of the o-carboranes is not only quenched by the presence of the Cc but that the fluorescence can also be tuned by changing the substituents on the Cc.
the Cc-Cf bond length plays a crucial role in the fluorescence intensity of the compounds studied.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in general, the Ccluster-Ccluster bonds are responsible for quenching the fluorescence of the anthracenyl and fluorenyl derivatives, but that the nature of the substituent on Ccluster may also have a significant impact on the fluorescence of the system.
the fluorescence of carborane derivatives can be modulated, and even turned off, by varying the fluorophore and its position in the carborane.
, depending on the type of the substituent on Cc (H, Me, Ph), the fluorescence of the anthracenyl derivative can be tuned from 0 to 94 %.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Ccluster (Ccluster= Cc, Cc-Cc) can be considered as an efficient fluorescence quencher, whereas the Ccluster (CC) is a very effective emitter.
the fluorescence of the o-carborane derivative can be controlled by the type of fluorophore, its position, and the substituents on the adjacent carbon atom of the Cc.
it is possible to design and synthesize o-carborane-based derivatives with different fluorophore fragments that can be tuned for different applications.
